title: Bookkeeping agency — e-commerce monthly close
summary: Reconcile a client's books to the cent every month. Pulls the bank feed daily, chases missing receipts, closes the month, prepares the sales tax return for your approval.

requires_connections.name: bank-feed
requires_connections.why: Pull the transactions daily so the month can actually be reconciled. Whichever of these you already use is fine.

requires_connections.name: accounting
requires_connections.why: The client's ledger — where the reconciled month is checked against what was actually invoiced.

requires_connections.name: books-email
requires_connections.why: Chase missing receipts and deliver the close report from an address your clients recognise.

schedules.name: month-end close
schedules._why_period: `monthly_close` declares `period` REQUIRED and says why in its own description: a close with no period is a close of nothing. This schedule carried an EMPTY input, so every scheduled close was exactly that — 3,077 runs across two engagements in a fortnight, one every 31 minutes, each asking for a period and a statement it was never given. The contract was declared and documented and nothing on this path read it. `{{month_ended}}` is filled by the clock at fire time; see schedule-input.ts for why the token lives in the manifest rather than as a branch in the scheduler.
schedules._why_not_this_month: A close fires on the 1st and covers the month BEFORE it. `{{this_month}}` would close a month still in progress, produce figures that change the next day, and hand a client a document that contradicts itself a week later.

# Engagement terms

Edit this with your actual terms. Example:
- Monthly close delivered by the 7th working day.
- Sales tax returns prepared, never filed without founder approval.
- Receipts chased up to 3 times, then escalated to the founder.
